nodes.coding_note: Criteria (Pathway §3.9): WBC ≥13×10⁹/L with immature myeloid cells ≥10% of WBC · PB/BM blasts <20% · dysgranulopoiesis · eosinophils <10% · monocytes <10% · hypercellular marrow with granulocytic hyperplasia and dysplasia · BCR::ABL1 and the M/LN-eo kinase fusions excluded. WHO-HAEM5 renames the entity "MDS/MPN with neutrophilia"; ICC keeps "atypical CML" — naming only, same code 9876 (Pathway §5.4).

options.label: All criteria met AND an MDS-qualifying cytopenia is present
options.coding_note: Both WHO-HAEM5 and ICC-2022 classify this case identically — no arbitration needed. BCR::ABL1 exclusion by FISH or RT-PCR discharges the molecular requirement.

options.label: All criteria met but there is NO MDS-qualifying cytopenia
options.coding_note: Divergent rule (Pathway §5.4). WHO-HAEM5 requires no cytopenia and classifies this as MDS/MPN with neutrophilia = 9876. ICC-2022 additionally requires an MDS-qualifying cytopenia and would not classify it as atypical CML. The registry codes 9876 and records which framework was applied.

options.label: Eosinophils are 10% or more of the WBC
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before any clonal eosinophilia code (9964–9968), document exclusion of parasitic infection and HIV. Unresolved secondary cause → do not code as a myeloid neoplasm.
options.coding_note: Eosinophils ≥10% fails an atypical CML criterion and opens the myeloid/lymphoid-neoplasm-with-eosinophilia cascade, which atypical CML explicitly excludes (Pathway §3.9, §3.10).

options.label: Monocytes are 10% or more of the WBC
options.coding_note: Monocytes ≥10% fails an atypical CML criterion and puts the case in CMML territory, owned by the MDS/JMML tree (Pathway §3.9, §7.1).

options.label: The PDGFRA / PDGFRB / FGFR1 / PCM1::JAK2 kinase fusions have NOT been excluded, or the dysplasia assessment is missing
options.upgrade_path: FISH or RT-PCR for the M/LN-eo kinase fusions, and a documented dysgranulopoiesis assessment, would establish or exclude 9876.
options.coding_note: Exclusion of the kinase fusions is part of the atypical CML definition. Until it is documented, 9876 is not defensible and 9960 is the honest NOS parent (Pathway §3.9, §6).

options.label: Reviewed — the neutrophilia is reactive or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: Reviewed as a reactive neutrophilia rather than atypical CML. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Total white cell count?
nodes.hint: Value in ×10⁹/L. Tick 'not documented' rather than guessing.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
nodes.coding_note: THE GATE IS A DISJUNCTION and the registry adopts BOTH routes (Pathway §3.9, §5.4). Route A — WBC ≥25×10⁹/L, no molecular test required (WHO-HAEM5; ICC too when CSF3R is negative). Route B — WBC ≥13×10⁹/L with an activating CSF3R mutation (ICC only). The shared criteria (neutrophils ≥80%, precursors <10%, no dysgranulopoiesis, monocytes <10%, blasts rare, normal maturation, BCR::ABL1/PV/ET/PMF/M-LN-eo excluded) were confirmed at the previous node.

override_when.coding_note: BCR::ABL1-positive disease is CML (9875), and its exclusion is a shared CNL criterion. A Ph-positive case can never be CNL, whatever the white count (Pathway §3.9).

bands.coding_note: Route A — count alone. WHO-HAEM5 accepts ≥25×10⁹/L unconditionally and ICC accepts it too when CSF3R is negative, so no molecular result is required. Phase is not a code here either: 10–19% blasts is accelerated phase, ≥20% is blast phase — both stay 9963.
Route B territory — ICC only, and only with an activating CSF3R mutation (or the ICC non-molecular alternative). WHO-HAEM5 would not call this CNL at all.

bands.upgrade_path: A repeat full blood count documenting persistent neutrophilia would establish whether either CNL route's threshold is met.
bands.coding_note: Below BOTH routes' thresholds — this is not CNL under either classification. If the marrow nonetheless documents a myeloproliferative process, 9960 is the honest code; if the neutrophilia is reactive, use the not-a-reportable-malignancy terminal on the previous node instead.

bands.upgrade_path: A full blood count with a differential would apply the CNL threshold and could resolve this to 9963.
bands.coding_note: The white count is the gate. Undocumented means the gate cannot be applied — 9960, not 9963.

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Chronic myeloproliferative picture recorded but no specific entity could be established. 9875 has no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code (Pathway §7.4).

nodes.question: WBC is 13–24×10⁹/L, so ICC route B applies. What does the file show for CSF3R?
nodes.hint: Route B is the only way to reach 9963 below 25×10⁹/L, and it is an ICC-2022 rule.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
nodes.coding_note: ICC route B: WBC ≥13×10⁹/L WITH an activating CSF3R mutation (typically T618I). ICC also allows a non-molecular alternative where CSF3R is unavailable: persistent neutrophilia for ≥3 months, splenomegaly, and reactive causes excluded — including demonstrated clonality if a plasma-cell neoplasm is present (Pathway §3.9).

options.finding: Activating CSF3R mutation present (e.g. T618I)
options.coding_note: ICC route B satisfied. WHO-HAEM5 would not classify this as CNL at this white count — record which framework was applied (Pathway §5.4).

options.finding: CSF3R unavailable, BUT persistent neutrophilia for ≥3 months, splenomegaly, and documented exclusion of reactive causes
options.coding_note: ICC's explicit non-molecular alternative for settings where CSF3R testing is not available (Pathway §3.9). The clinical constellation discharges the molecular requirement; record that CSF3R itself was never performed.

options.finding: CSF3R tested and NEGATIVE
options.upgrade_path: None on this route. ICC requires ≥25×10⁹/L when CSF3R is negative; a rising white count on repeat testing would re-open the CNL question.
options.coding_note: CSF3R-negative at 13–24×10⁹/L fails BOTH routes — ICC then requires ≥25×10⁹/L, and WHO-HAEM5 always does. 9963 is not defensible; 9960 is the honest NOS parent (Pathway §3.9).

options.finding: CSF3R not performed, and the non-molecular alternative is not documented
options.upgrade_path: CSF3R sequencing, or documentation of ≥3 months of neutrophilia with splenomegaly and reactive causes excluded, would establish 9963 on ICC route B.
options.coding_note: Route B is unestablished. "Molecular unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate permanent terminal state but must be recorded as such (Pathway §2.5).

options.finding: Reviewed — the neutrophilia has a documented reactive cause (infection, chronic inflammation, corticosteroids, G-CSF)
options.reason: The neutrophilia is reactive. Exclusion of reactive causes is a shared CNL criterion under both classifications, so this is not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §3.9, §4.9).

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Chronic myeloproliferative picture recorded but no specific entity could be established. 9875 has no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code (Pathway §7.4).

nodes.question: Which phenotype-plus-driver combination does the file document?
nodes.hint: Each of these entities needs BOTH a phenotype threshold and a driver mutation. One without the other does not reach the code.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
nodes.coding_note: Polycythaemia vera, essential thrombocythaemia and primary myelofibrosis are vanishingly rare in children (Pathway §1, Ic). They stay reachable — removing them would make a genuine rare paediatric case uncodeable — but every option carries the age-implausibility warning and should be confirmed independently before finalising (Pathway §7.5).

options.finding: Erythrocytosis above threshold (Hb >16.5 g/dL male / >16.0 g/dL female, or Hct >49% male / >48% female) WITH a JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon-12 mutation
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
options.coding_note: Polycythaemia vera. Paediatric erythrocytosis is far more often congenital (EPO-receptor, high-affinity haemoglobin, hypoxia) — a JAK2 mutation is what separates PV from those, and it is required here.

options.finding: Platelets ≥450×10⁹/L WITH a JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
options.coding_note: Essential thrombocythaemia. Reactive thrombocytosis — iron deficiency, infection, inflammation, post-splenectomy — is far commoner in children and is excluded by the driver requirement.

options.finding: Trephine megakaryocyte atypia with a GRADED reticulin / collagen stain WITH a JAK2, CALR or MPL mutation
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
options.coding_note: Primary myelofibrosis. The trephine and the graded reticulin stain are both required — an aspirate alone cannot support this code.

options.finding: The phenotype is present but the JAK2 / CALR / MPL panel was NEGATIVE or was not performed
options.upgrade_path: A JAK2 V617F and exon-12, CALR and MPL panel would resolve this to 9950, 9961 or 9962.
options.coding_note: A driver mutation is required for all three entities. Triple-negative primary myelofibrosis exists in adults but needs another clonal marker plus exclusion of reactive marrow fibrosis — in a child, refer for senior review and use the uncertain-subtype escape rather than assuming it. 9960 is the honest code here.

options.finding: Reviewed — secondary or reactive erythrocytosis, thrombocytosis or marrow fibrosis (hypoxia, congenital polycythaemia, iron deficiency, infection, inflammation, post-splenectomy)
options.reason: The blood or marrow finding has a documented reactive or congenital cause. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nos_fallback.name: Myeloproliferative neoplasm, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Chronic myeloproliferative picture recorded but no specific entity could be established. 9875 has no valid downgrade to a lesser CML code (Pathway §7.4).

nodes.question: HARD GATE. Before ANY clonal-eosinophilia code, the file must document exclusion of parasitic infection AND HIV. What does it show?
nodes.hint: This gate is not optional and cannot be skipped. Answer from what is written in the file, not from clinical impression.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before any clonal eosinophilia code (9964–9968), document exclusion of parasitic infection and HIV. Unresolved secondary cause → do not code as a myeloid neoplasm.
nodes.coding_note: STEP 1 OF THE CASCADE IS A HARD GATE (Pathway §3.10, §5.6). Secondary causes to exclude: parasitic (strongyloides, schistosoma, filariasis, hookworm, toxocara), HIV, drugs, allergy, autoimmune disease and solid-tumour-associated eosinophilia. In the UCI catchment hypereosinophilia is overwhelmingly parasitic or HIV-related; skipping this step is the largest single false-positive cancer-registration risk in Group I. An unresolved secondary cause must reach a non-reportable terminal, never a myeloid-neoplasm code.

options.label: BOTH excluded and documented — stool microscopy and/or serology negative for the parasitic set, AND an HIV test is negative; drugs, allergy, autoimmune disease and solid tumour also considered
options.coding_note: The hard gate is satisfied. Only now do the clonal-eosinophilia codes (9964–9968) become reachable.

options.label: A secondary cause has been IDENTIFIED — parasitic infection, HIV, a drug reaction, allergy, autoimmune disease or a solid tumour
options.reason: The hypereosinophilia has a documented secondary cause. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. This is the commonest false-positive registration risk in Group I in the UCI catchment (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Parasitic infection excluded, but HIV status is unknown or not tested
options.coding_note: Half a gate is not a gate. HIV-associated eosinophilia is common in this catchment and the exclusion must be documented before any clonal code.

options.label: HIV excluded, but no parasitic screen has been performed
options.coding_note: Half a gate is not a gate. The parasitic screen must be documented before any clonal code.

options.label: Neither has been assessed
options.coding_note: The gate has not been attempted. No clonal-eosinophilia code is reachable from here.

nodes.question: The secondary-cause exclusion is incomplete, so no myeloid-neoplasm code can be emitted. What is the status of the missing test?
nodes.hint: This branch deliberately cannot reach a morphology code. It exists so the case is recorded honestly and can be re-entered when the screen is done.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before any clonal eosinophilia code (9964–9968), document exclusion of parasitic infection and HIV. Unresolved secondary cause → do not code as a myeloid neoplasm.
nodes.coding_note: An unresolved secondary cause must reach a NON-REPORTABLE terminal, not a myeloid-neoplasm code (Pathway §3.10, §5.6, §4.9). Coding 9964–9968 here would register a cancer that has not been established. If a senior pathologist judges the case neoplastic on other grounds, use the uncertain-subtype escape hatch rather than this branch.

options.label: The parasitic screen / HIV test is now available — go back and enter the result
Screening requested — result pending
options.reason: The secondary-cause exclusion required before any clonal-eosinophilia code is still pending. Not reportable on the present evidence — no code is emitted. Re-enter the tool when the parasitic screen and HIV result return (Pathway §3.10).

options.label: Screening not available at this facility
options.reason: The parasitic screen and/or HIV test that the hard gate requires is unavailable, so a secondary cause cannot be excluded. Not reportable — no code is emitted. In this catchment an unexcluded secondary cause is far more likely than a clonal eosinophilic neoplasm (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

nodes.question: Secondary causes are excluded. What clonality evidence does the file contain?
nodes.hint: Idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome and a clonal eosinophilic neoplasm look identical on the film — clonality is what separates them.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Cryptic deletion. Do not assign 9964 or exclude 9965 on a normal karyotype — FISH (CHIC2 deletion) or RT-PCR required.
nodes.coding_note: Cascade step 5 is asked BEFORE the fusion dropdown, because the dropdown's NOS fallback is 9964 and 9964 requires demonstrated clonality (ICC, Pathway §5.4). Without clonality the case is idiopathic HES and is NOT REPORTABLE (Pathway §3.10, §4.9). A normal karyotype is not "tested and normal" for this purpose — FIP1L1::PDGFRA is cryptic and needs FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR.

options.label: A clonal abnormality is demonstrated, or specific fusion testing has been performed — an abnormal karyotype, a kinase fusion, another clonal molecular marker, or an increased blast count
options.coding_note: Clonality established (or specific fusion testing done). The cascade can now resolve the specific entity.

options.label: Karyotype normal, but FISH for the CHIC2 deletion / RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA has NOT been performed
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Cryptic deletion. Do not assign 9964 or exclude 9965 on a normal karyotype — FISH (CHIC2 deletion) or RT-PCR required.
options.coding_note: A normal karyotype closes nothing here. FIP1L1::PDGFRA is a cryptic deletion, invisible on karyotype, and the resulting disease is imatinib-responsive — the most consequential miss in this branch (Pathway §4.4, §5.6).

options.label: Cytogenetics AND molecular testing performed and completely normal — including FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA — with no clonal marker and no increased blasts
options.reason: Persistent hypereosinophilia with secondary causes excluded and no demonstrable clonality is idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome. HES is not a malignancy — no code is emitted, and in particular not 9964 (Pathway §3.10 step 5, §4.9).

options.label: No cytogenetic or molecular testing has been performed at all
Reviewed — the hypereosinophilia is reactive or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: Reviewed as reactive or non-neoplastic hypereosinophilia. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: No clonality testing has been done. What is its status?
nodes.hint: Untested is not the same as negative — but neither is it evidence of a neoplasm.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Cryptic deletion. Do not assign 9964 or exclude 9965 on a normal karyotype — FISH (CHIC2 deletion) or RT-PCR required.
nodes.coding_note: CEL (9964) requires demonstrated clonality under the registry's ratified ICC criteria (Pathway §5.4). With no testing at all, clonality is unestablished and the case cannot be coded as a myeloid neoplasm; the honest record is a non-reportable terminal naming the missing tests. If a senior pathologist judges the case neoplastic on other grounds, use the uncertain-subtype escape hatch, which lands on the nearest NOS code with a discordance flag.

options.label: Karyotype / FISH / RT-PCR now available — go back and enter the result
Testing requested — result pending
options.reason: Clonality is unestablished and the fusion cascade is untested. Not reportable on the present evidence — no code is emitted. Re-enter the tool when the karyotype, FISH (CHIC2) or RT-PCR result returns (Pathway §3.10).

options.label: Cytogenetics and molecular testing not available at this facility
options.reason: Clonality cannot be demonstrated at this facility, and CEL (9964) requires demonstrated clonality. Recorded as not reportable with the missing tests named, rather than as an unproven myeloid neoplasm (Pathway §3.10, §4.9, §5.4).

nodes.question: Which finding does the cytogenetics / FISH / molecular report give?
nodes.hint: Work down the list in order. The detection method shown under each choice is the method that finding actually requires.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Cryptic deletion. Do not assign 9964 or exclude 9965 on a normal karyotype — FISH (CHIC2 deletion) or RT-PCR required.
nodes.coding_note: Cascade order (Pathway §3.10): FIP1L1::PDGFRA → 9965, then karyotype 5q31-33 PDGFRB → 9966 and 8p11-12 FGFR1 → 9967, then PCM1::JAK2 → 9968, then clonality without a named fusion → 9964. The secondary-cause hard gate and the clonality gate are both upstream of this node and cannot be bypassed.

options.finding: FIP1L1::PDGFRA — CHIC2 deletion on FISH, or RT-PCR positive (or another PDGFRA rearrangement with a variant partner)
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Cryptic deletion. Do not assign 9964 or exclude 9965 on a normal karyotype — FISH (CHIC2 deletion) or RT-PCR required.
options.coding_note: CRYPTIC — never visible on karyotype. Only FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR can establish or exclude it, and either method alone is sufficient. Clinically the most important call in this branch: these cases are imatinib-responsive (Pathway §4.4, §5.6).

options.finding: PDGFRB rearrangement — 5q31-33 abnormality on karyotype, confirmed by FISH
options.coding_note: Visible on karyotype as a 5q31-33 rearrangement; FISH confirms the partner. Also imatinib-responsive.

options.finding: FGFR1 abnormality — 8p11-12 rearrangement on karyotype, confirmed by FISH
options.coding_note: 8p11-12 myeloproliferative syndrome. Not imatinib-responsive — the distinction from PDGFRA/PDGFRB matters clinically as well as for coding.

options.finding: PCM1::JAK2 — t(8;9)(p22;p24) on karyotype, or FISH, or RT-PCR positive
options.coding_note: 9968 became a live ICD-O-3.2 code at the 3.2 revision and was previously (and wrongly) advised to 9964 (Pathway §5.7). REGISTRY ACTION OUTSTANDING: no REDCap dropdown option exists for this code yet, so the clerk cannot select it in REDCap until one is added.

options.finding: ETV6::ABL1, a FLT3 fusion, or another kinase fusion with no dedicated ICD-O-3.2 code
options.coding_note: No ICD-O-3.2 code exists for these. They land provisionally on 9964 with the genotype preserved, or the information is lost permanently (Pathway §5.2).

options.finding: Karyotype abnormal or blasts increased, but FISH for the CHIC2 deletion / RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA NOT performed
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Cryptic deletion. Do not assign 9964 or exclude 9965 on a normal karyotype — FISH (CHIC2 deletion) or RT-PCR required.
options.coding_note: Clonality is established but the cryptic branch is still open. Do not resolve to 9964 yet — a normal or non-specific karyotype does not exclude 9965 (Pathway §4.4, §5.6).

options.finding: Karyotype done AND FISH / RT-PCR negative for the whole kinase-fusion set, with clonality shown by another marker or by increased blasts
options.coding_note: Chronic eosinophilic leukaemia, NOS — the properly closed terminal. Registry applies ICC criteria for CEL versus HES: ≥10% peripheral eosinophils, clonality required, blast increase supportive (Pathway §5.4). The cryptic branch has been closed by an adequate method, so this is a defensible terminal and not an incomplete workup.

nos_fallback.name: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Clonal hypereosinophilia with the secondary causes excluded, but no specific kinase fusion identified.

nodes.question: A normal karyotype cannot exclude FIP1L1::PDGFRA. Has FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR been performed since?
nodes.hint: This branch deliberately cannot close to 9964. It closes to the MPN NOS parent only with the missing test named on the record.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Cryptic deletion. Do not assign 9964 or exclude 9965 on a normal karyotype — FISH (CHIC2 deletion) or RT-PCR required.
nodes.coding_note: FIP1L1::PDGFRA arises from an interstitial 4q12 deletion that removes CHIC2 — there is no karyotypic abnormality to see. A normal karyotype must never close this branch, and must never resolve to 9964 (Pathway §4.4, §5.6, §7.5).

options.label: FISH (CHIC2) / RT-PCR now available — go back and enter the result
FISH / RT-PCR requested — result pending
FISH / RT-PCR not available at this facility

nodes.question: Record why FIP1L1::PDGFRA could not be tested. The case codes 9960 with the missing test named.
nodes.hint: 9960, not 9964: the alert forbids assigning 9964 on a normal karyotype, so the case steps one rung further up the chain instead.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Cryptic deletion. Do not assign 9964 or exclude 9965 on a normal karyotype — FISH (CHIC2 deletion) or RT-PCR required.
nodes.coding_note: The eosinophilic fallback chain is 9965 / 9966 / 9967 → 9964 → 9960 (Pathway §6). 9964 is unavailable here because "do not assign 9964 ... on a normal karyotype" is an explicit alert (Pathway §5.6), so the honest terminal is the next rung, 9960, with karyotype_result_status recording why.

options.label: Pending — record now and re-enter the tool when the result returns
options.upgrade_path: FISH for the CHIC2 deletion or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA would upgrade this to 9965; if negative with clonality shown, to 9964. Result pending — re-enter when it returns.
options.coding_note: Do not treat this as a settled 9960. The FIP1L1::PDGFRA branch is still open, and that diagnosis is imatinib-responsive.

options.label: Not available at this facility — permanent terminal state
options.upgrade_path: FISH (CHIC2) and RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA are unavailable; the code cannot be upgraded at this facility.
options.coding_note: Recorded as a permanent unavailable-workup terminal, not as an excluded cryptic set. Consider referral for testing if imatinib is a realistic option.

options.label: Test declined or not done for another reason
options.upgrade_path: FISH (CHIC2) or RT-PCR for FIP1L1::PDGFRA would upgrade this code; the test was not done.

nodes.question: Record the fusion exactly as the report states it.
nodes.capture_label: Genotype as reported (e.g. "ETV6::ABL1 by RT-PCR", "FLT3 fusion, partner not stated")
nodes.hint: The code does not change, but the genotype is preserved on the case record.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before any clonal eosinophilia code (9964–9968), document exclusion of parasitic infection and HIV. Unresolved secondary cause → do not code as a myeloid neoplasm.
nodes.coding_note: ETV6::ABL1 and the FLT3-fusion myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms have no dedicated ICD-O-3.2 code and land provisionally on 9964 (Pathway §5.2). The annotation is always persisted, even though the finding is code-neutral — otherwise the entity is lost permanently.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Provisional landing code. The secondary-cause hard gate and the clonality gate are both satisfied upstream, and the fusion itself demonstrates clonality.
resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None — no ICD-O-3.2 code exists for this entity. The genotype is preserved on the case record instead; revisit if a future ICD-O revision codes it.

nos_fallback.name: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Clonal hypereosinophilia with the secondary causes excluded, but no specific kinase fusion identified.

decision_trees.tree_label: Myelodysplastic syndromes, JMML and MDS/MPN overlap

nodes.question: What reports are in this patient's file? Pick the highest tier available, or the special context that applies.
nodes.hint: This is the evidence gate. It fixes what precision is achievable and drives every 'upgrade available' line on the output block.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Group I has no imaging-sufficient route — imaging is staging only (Pathway §0). A case that arrived here from the acute tree's blast gate enters at mds_eb_pediatric_entry or mds_rcc_entry instead and skips this node.

options.label: Referral / clinical note only — no marrow report
Blood film / marrow aspirate morphology only (no trephine, no IHC, no cytogenetics)
Marrow aspirate + trephine biopsy with IHC (CD61 / CD41 performed)
options.coding_note: CD61 or CD41 IHC on the trephine is mandatory in paediatric MDS — it identifies the micromegakaryocytes that separate refractory cytopenia of childhood from severe aplastic anaemia (Pathway §3.5).

options.label: Marrow + trephine/IHC + cytogenetics / FISH
Marrow + trephine/IHC + cytogenetics + molecular / PCR / NGS
Monocytosis-predominant picture — persistent monocytosis with or without splenomegaly (JMML / CMML suspicion)
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Germline PTPN11 without a somatic secondary lesion is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML. Confirm a somatic RAS-pathway lesion before coding 9946.
options.coding_note: JMML is the flagship paediatric Group I MDS/MPN entity. Monocytosis alone is not a diagnosis — reactive monocytosis (TB, HIV, other chronic infection) is the commonest cause in the UCI catchment and must reach a non-reportable terminal (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Hypereosinophilia is the dominant finding, not monocytosis or dysplasia
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before any clonal eosinophilia code (9964–9967), document exclusion of parasitic infection and HIV. Unresolved secondary cause → do not code as a myeloid neoplasm.
options.coding_note: The eosinophilia cascade (9964–9968) belongs to the chronic myeloid / MPN tree, not to this one (Pathway §3.10, §7.1). Do not code a clonal eosinophilia terminal from the MDS/JMML tree — exclude parasitic infection and HIV first, then re-enter at the chronic myeloid / MPN tree.

options.label: Malignancy excluded on review — reactive, non-neoplastic or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: The abstractor recorded that this case is not a reportable malignancy. No morphology code is emitted and the case leaves the malignant registry.

nodes.question: What exactly does the referral or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: A referral naming an entity is not the same as a marrow report establishing it. The wording chooses the NOS parent, never the specific code.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Germline PTPN11 without a somatic secondary lesion is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML. Confirm a somatic RAS-pathway lesion before coding 9946.
nodes.coding_note: Referral-only tier: confidence is LOW and every downstream test is listed as an upgrade. 9946 and 9985 are never emitted from this node — both require marrow evidence the file does not contain (Pathway §3.4, §3.5).

options.label: Note reads "myelodysplastic syndrome", "MDS", "myelodysplasia" or "preleukaemia" — no marrow report
options.upgrade_path: A marrow aspirate and trephine with CD61/CD41 IHC would separate 9985 (refractory cytopenia of childhood) from 9983 (excess blasts); cytogenetics would add 9986.
options.coding_note: 9989 is the honest referral-tier code. Do not assume 9985 — the commonest paediatric MDS is still a marrow diagnosis.

options.label: Note reads "refractory anaemia", "RAEB", "RARS" or another FAB-era term — no marrow report
options.upgrade_path: A marrow aspirate with a blast count and a trephine would establish the WHO/ICC subtype.
options.coding_note: FAB terms in a referral do not carry a blast count. 9980/9982/9983 all require the marrow report.

options.label: Note reads "JMML", "juvenile myelomonocytic leukaemia" or "juvenile chronic myeloid leukaemia" — no marrow and no molecular report
options.upgrade_path: A marrow report (blasts <20%), BCR::ABL1 exclusion by FISH/RT-PCR and a RAS-pathway panel (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, RRAS, NF1, CBL) would establish 9946.
options.coding_note: 9946 requires a somatic RAS-pathway lesion (Pathway §3.4). A referral naming JMML is not that evidence — 9975 is the MDS/MPN NOS parent in the §6 fallback chain (9945 / 9946 → 9975 → 9800).

options.label: Note reads "CMML", "chronic myelomonocytic leukaemia" or "chronic monocytic leukaemia" — no marrow report
options.upgrade_path: A monocyte count (absolute and as % of WBC), a marrow blast count and evidence of dysplasia or clonality would establish 9945.
options.coding_note: CMML needs the two-tier monocyte rule of Pathway §3.10 before 9945 is defensible. 9975 is the NOS parent.

options.label: Note reads "MDS/MPN overlap" or "myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable"
options.upgrade_path: A marrow report with a blast count, monocyte count and cytogenetics would establish 9945, 9946 or a specific MDS subtype.

options.label: Note reads "therapy-related MDS" / "t-MDS" after prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Prior cytotoxic therapy is a qualifier on the underlying neoplasm (ELN 2022), not a separate entity. Code the underlying subtype and set the qualifier rather than defaulting to 9920/9987.
options.upgrade_path: A marrow report would establish the underlying MDS subtype, which is the code; the therapy relationship stays a qualifier.
options.coding_note: DO NOT CODE 9987. Therapy-related MDS is a QUALIFIER on the underlying diagnosis, not a terminal (Pathway §4.8, §5.3.7). 9987 and 9920 are closed as terminals.

options.label: Note reads only "pancytopenia", "bone marrow failure" or "anaemia under investigation" — no malignant diagnosis is asserted
options.reason: The referral asserts a cytopenia, not a malignancy. No morphology code is emitted; the case is not entered on the malignant registry until a marrow report establishes a neoplasm.

nodes.question: What does the marrow aspirate / blood film report describe?
nodes.hint: Iron stain (ring sideroblasts) and cytochemistry count as morphology. A trephine with CD61/CD41 IHC does not — that is the next tier up.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Morphology-only tier. The mandatory paediatric pre-conditions (reversible causes, prior therapy, germline predisposition, IBMFS) are still unasked — every dysplastic option routes into that chain rather than terminating here.

options.label: Cytopenia(s) with dysplasia — marrow blasts under 5%
Cytopenia(s) with dysplasia — marrow blasts 5–19%
Persistent monocytosis with a myeloproliferative picture — circulating myeloid precursors, splenomegaly
Dysplasia described; blast count not stated and no further investigation is possible at this facility
options.upgrade_path: A blast count would separate 9983 from 9985; a trephine with CD61/CD41 IHC would exclude aplastic anaemia; cytogenetics would add 9986.
options.coding_note: A permanent LMIC terminal state, recorded as such. The §5.6 pre-conditions were not documented — germline_predisposition and ibmfs_exclusion_status stay 'not tested' on the output block.

options.label: Marrow reviewed — megaloblastic / reactive change, not dysplasia
options.reason: Marrow morphology showed reactive or megaloblastic change rather than a dysplastic clone. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Which pattern does the marrow aspirate and trephine describe?
nodes.hint: Pick the dominant pattern. The blast count is confirmed later, at the gate that actually fixes the code.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Group I has no site resolution — the marrow pattern plus the blast band does the work topography does in solid-tumour groups (Pathway §2.2).

options.descriptor: Monocytosis with myeloproliferative features — splenomegaly, leucocytosis, circulating myeloid precursors
Cytopenia(s) with dysplasia — marrow blasts under 5% and peripheral blasts under 2%
Cytopenia(s) with dysplasia and increased blasts — marrow 5–19%, peripheral 2–19%
options.coding_note: Paediatric MDS with excess blasts is the 5–19% band under ICC. ICC's separate MDS/AML 10–19% category is explicitly excluded under 18 years (Pathway §5.4).

options.descriptor: Ring sideroblasts prominent on the iron stain, with dysplasia
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
options.coding_note: Ring-sideroblast entities (9982, 9993) are adult-predominant — <1% of paediatric MDS. They stay reachable; the age-implausibility warning travels with them (Pathway §7.5).

options.descriptor: Hypocellular marrow with cytopenias — refractory cytopenia of childhood versus severe aplastic anaemia not yet separated
options.coding_note: About 80% of refractory cytopenia of childhood is hypocellular. CD61/CD41 IHC on the trephine is the discriminator (Pathway §3.5).

options.descriptor: Overlapping myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features — the CMML, atypical CML and JMML criteria are all unmet
Dysplasia documented but the subtype is not stated in the report
Marrow reviewed — no dysplasia, no excess blasts and no clonal population
options.reason: The marrow shows neither dysplasia nor a clonal population. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Absolute peripheral-blood monocyte count?
nodes.hint: Absolute count in ×10⁹/L. The relative criterion (≥10% of WBC) is asked at the next step. Tick 'not documented' rather than guessing — monocytosis is absent in about 7% of true JMML.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Germline PTPN11 without a somatic secondary lesion is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML. Confirm a somatic RAS-pathway lesion before coding 9946.
nodes.coding_note: ≥1×10⁹/L is the JMML clinical criterion and the CMML one-supporting-criterion tier; 0.5–<1×10⁹/L is the CMML two-supporting-criteria tier (Pathway §3.4, §3.10).

override_when.coding_note: Blasts ≥20% — this is acute leukaemia, not an MDS/MPN. Blasts <20% in both blood and marrow is a MANDATORY JMML criterion (Pathway §3.4); the case belongs in the acute tree.

bands.coding_note: Meets the JMML monocyte criterion and the CMML ≥1×10⁹/L tier. Reactive monocytosis must be excluded first, especially at this level (Pathway §3.10).
CMML two-tier rule: at 0.5–<1×10⁹/L BOTH supporting criteria are required — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage AND clonal cytogenetic/molecular evidence.
Below the monocytosis threshold under both WHO-HAEM5 and ICC — neither CMML nor the JMML monocyte criterion is met. Assess the case as a myelodysplastic syndrome on its marrow pattern instead.
Monocyte count not documented. Monocytosis is absent in about 7% of true JMML, so an undocumented count does not close the JMML branch — it is the genetics that decide (Pathway §3.4).

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable.
nos_fallback.reason: MDS/MPN overlap picture recorded but the CMML, aCML and JMML criteria were not met or could not be established.

nodes.question: Is the monocytosis persistent, and have reactive causes been excluded and documented?
nodes.hint: Persistence means ≥3 months unless a clonal marker is already present. In the UCI catchment tuberculosis and HIV are the commonest causes of a persistent monocytosis.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Reactive monocytosis (tuberculosis, HIV, other chronic infection, marrow recovery, G-CSF) is not a malignancy. It must reach a non-reportable terminal, never an NOS malignant code (Pathway §4.9).
nodes.coding_note: CMUS / CCMUS — persistent monocytosis ≥10% of WBC and ≥0.5×10⁹/L with the CMML criteria unmet — is explicitly not malignant and must not be reported (Pathway §3.10).

options.label: Persistent monocytosis, ≥10% of the white cell count, reactive causes excluded and documented
Reactive cause identified — tuberculosis, HIV, other chronic infection, marrow recovery or G-CSF
options.reason: The monocytosis is reactive (infection, marrow recovery or growth-factor effect). Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

options.label: Persistent monocytosis but under 10% of the white cell count, or the CMML criteria are otherwise unmet — CMUS / CCMUS
options.reason: Clonal or idiopathic monocytosis of undetermined significance (CMUS/CCMUS). Explicitly not malignant and must not be reported (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Splenomegaly and cytopenias fully explained by malaria or HIV hypersplenism
options.reason: Hypersplenism from malaria or HIV accounts for the splenomegaly and cytopenias, and confounds the JMML criteria. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

options.label: Reactive causes not yet assessed — the file does not document the exclusions
options.coding_note: Recorded as an incomplete exclusion. It does not change the code, but it is the single largest false-positive registration risk in this group and must appear on the output block.

nodes.question: Which entity does the marrow and clinical picture describe?
nodes.hint: Age is not diagnostic for JMML — it is prognostic only (Pathway §3.4). The genetics decide, not the age.
nodes.coding_note: JMML (9946) and CMML (9945) share a monocytic phenotype and separate on the RAS-pathway lesion and the supporting-criteria rule, not on age.

options.descriptor: Myeloproliferative picture — splenomegaly, elevated HbF for age, circulating myeloid precursors, monosomy 7 (JMML pattern)
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Germline PTPN11 without a somatic secondary lesion is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML. Confirm a somatic RAS-pathway lesion before coding 9946.

options.descriptor: Dysplastic monocytic picture — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage and/or a clonal marker, no splenomegaly-led myeloproliferative picture (CMML pattern)
Overlapping myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features — the CMML, atypical CML and JMML criteria are all unmet
Blasts ≥20% in blood or marrow — an acute picture
options.coding_note: Blasts <20% in both blood and marrow is a MANDATORY JMML criterion and bounds CMML too. At ≥20% the case is acute leukaemia and belongs in the acute tree (Pathway §3.4, §3.10).

nodes.question: Two JMML criteria are MANDATORY: blasts under 20% in blood and marrow, and documented absence of BCR::ABL1. What does the file show?
nodes.hint: 'Absence of BCR::ABL1' means a negative FISH or RT-PCR result in the file. A normal karyotype is not that result.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ BCR::ABL1 must be EXCLUDED before 9946 is emitted — it is a mandatory JMML criterion (Pathway §3.4). If BCR::ABL1 is POSITIVE this is chronic myeloid leukaemia, not JMML — take the BCR::ABL1-positive branch below, which hands the case to the chronic myeloid / MPN tree. Do not code 9946 and do not code an MDS terminal.
nodes.coding_note: Category I criteria (Pathway §3.4): PB monocytes ≥1×10⁹/L (absent in ~7%), splenomegaly (absent in ~3%), blasts <20% — MANDATORY, absence of BCR::ABL1 — MANDATORY. Only the last two are hard gates.

options.label: BCR::ABL1 excluded — FISH or RT-PCR negative — and blasts under 20% in both blood and marrow
BCR::ABL1 POSITIVE — Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) on karyotype, or BCR::ABL1 detected by FISH or RT-PCR
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ A Ph-positive monocytic picture is chronic myeloid leukaemia, not JMML and not CMML. BCR::ABL1 positive codes 9875 regardless of phase (Pathway §3.9).
options.coding_note: The mandatory JMML criterion fails in the POSITIVE direction, which is diagnostic rather than merely disqualifying. Monocytosis in a Ph-positive case does not make it CMML: the case is owned by the chronic myeloid / MPN tree (Pathway §7.1), which resolves BCR::ABL1-positive disease to 9875 and records the phase as a display-only qualifier. Do not code 9946, 9945 or any MDS terminal here.

options.label: Blasts under 20% but BCR::ABL1 not tested, or the result is not in the file
options.coding_note: A mandatory criterion is unestablished. 9946 cannot be emitted on this evidence — the case lands on the MDS/MPN NOS parent with the missing tests listed as upgrades (Pathway §3.4, §6 fallback chain).

options.label: Blasts 20% or more in blood or marrow
options.coding_note: The mandatory blast criterion fails. This is acute leukaemia — assign lineage in the acute tree.

options.label: Reviewed — the monocytosis, splenomegaly and cytopenias are fully explained by malaria or HIV hypersplenism
options.reason: Hypersplenism from malaria or HIV accounts for the whole picture and confounds the JMML criteria. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Which supporting findings does the file document?
nodes.hint: Supporting criteria are recorded, not decisive. Category II — a RAS-pathway lesion — is what establishes JMML, and it is asked next.
nodes.coding_note: Supporting criteria (Pathway §3.4): HbF elevated for age, circulating myeloid precursors, monosomy 7. None of them changes the code; all of them belong on the output block.

options.label: Splenomegaly present and HbF elevated for age
Splenomegaly present, HbF normal or not tested
No splenomegaly — HbF elevated for age and/or circulating myeloid precursors present
options.coding_note: Splenomegaly is absent in about 3% of true JMML. Its absence does not close the branch.

options.label: Monosomy 7 on cytogenetics, with or without splenomegaly
options.coding_note: Monosomy 7 is supporting, not defining. It is also the commonest cytogenetic abnormality in refractory cytopenia of childhood (~20%) — it does not by itself choose between 9946 and 9985.

options.label: None of the supporting findings is documented

nodes.question: What does the molecular / cytogenetic report show on the RAS pathway?
nodes.hint: Category II requires at least one of these, and it is present in over 95% of true JMML. The distinction that matters is SOMATIC versus germline-only.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Germline PTPN11 without a somatic secondary lesion is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML. Confirm a somatic RAS-pathway lesion before coding 9946.
nodes.coding_note: DNA-methylation subgroups (low / intermediate / high) are prognostic and code-neutral — all remain 9946. Spontaneous regression (~15%, germline CBL and some NRAS G12S) does not retract the diagnosis: code at diagnosis on the evidence then available (Pathway §3.4, §5.3.9).

options.finding: Somatic PTPN11 mutation (marrow, not germline)
options.coding_note: Somatic PTPN11 is the commonest JMML lesion. Confirm it is somatic — a germline PTPN11 variant alone is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML.

options.finding: Somatic KRAS mutation
Somatic NRAS mutation
options.coding_note: Some NRAS G12S cases regress spontaneously. Regression is a follow-up fact, not a coding fact — the case stays an incident registration (Pathway §5.3.9).

options.finding: Somatic RRAS mutation
Germline NF1 with loss of heterozygosity, or clinical neurofibromatosis type 1 (≥6 café-au-lait macules over 5 mm)
options.coding_note: Clinical NF1 satisfies Category II without a molecular NF1 report. Record the germline finding as a qualifier on the output block.

options.finding: Germline CBL with loss of heterozygosity
options.coding_note: Germline CBL JMML regresses spontaneously in a substantial minority. It is still an incident case coded at diagnosis (Pathway §5.3.9).

options.finding: Germline PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS or RIT1 ONLY — no somatic secondary lesion, normal karyotype
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Germline PTPN11 without a somatic secondary lesion is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML. Confirm a somatic RAS-pathway lesion before coding 9946.
options.coding_note: Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferative disease. Distinct from JMML and usually self-limiting — do NOT auto-code 9946 (Pathway §3.4, §4.9, §5.6).

options.finding: RAS-pathway panel performed — no lesion identified; an ALK, ROS1, FIP1L1::RARA or CCDC88C::FLT3 fusion, or nothing at all
options.coding_note: ICC-2022's RAS-negative 'JMML-like neoplasm' is NOT adopted (registry decision, Pathway §5.3.2 and §5.4). It has no ICD-O-3.2 code and is coded 9975 on its own merits, with the fusion preserved in genotype_annotation.

options.finding: Monosomy 7 only — no RAS-pathway lesion on a panel that was performed
options.coding_note: Monosomy 7 is supporting, never defining. Without a Category II lesion the case is not JMML.

options.finding: Molecular testing not performed, or unavailable at this facility
options.upgrade_path: A RAS-pathway panel (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, RRAS, NF1, CBL, with germline/somatic discrimination) would establish or exclude 9946.
options.coding_note: Category II is unestablished, so 9946 cannot be emitted — the case lands on the MDS/MPN NOS parent (Pathway §6 fallback chain: 9945 / 9946 → 9975 → 9800). "Molecular unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate permanent terminal state, but it must be recorded as such.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable.
nos_fallback.reason: MDS/MPN overlap picture recorded but the CMML, aCML and JMML criteria were not met or could not be established.

nodes.question: Record exactly what molecular or cytogenetic testing the file does contain, and what it showed.
nodes.capture_label: Testing as reported (e.g. "karyotype 46,XY; no FISH, no RAS panel", "no molecular testing performed")
nodes.hint: A mandatory JMML criterion is unestablished. This node records why, so the upgrade line on the output block is accurate.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Germline PTPN11 without a somatic secondary lesion is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML. Confirm a somatic RAS-pathway lesion before coding 9946.
nodes.coding_note: A JMML with no molecular testing must NOT reach 9946 (Pathway §8 scenario list). 9975 is the honest terminal — the MDS/MPN NOS parent — with the missing tests listed as upgrades.

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: BCR::ABL1 by FISH or RT-PCR, and a RAS-pathway panel (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, RRAS, NF1, CBL), would establish or exclude 9946.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Absence of BCR::ABL1 is a MANDATORY JMML criterion and it is unestablished here. 9946 is not emitted (Pathway §3.4).

resolution_logic.upgrade_path: A RAS-pathway panel (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS, RRAS, NF1, CBL) would establish or exclude 9946.
resolution_logic.coding_note: Category II is unestablished. 9975 on its own merits, genotype preserved.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable.
nos_fallback.reason: MDS/MPN overlap picture recorded but the CMML, aCML and JMML criteria were not met or could not be established.

nodes.question: A germline RASopathy variant is present. Has a SOMATIC secondary lesion been documented on the marrow?
nodes.hint: Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferative disease has a germline variant, no somatic second hit, a normal karyotype and a self-limiting course.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Germline PTPN11 without a somatic secondary lesion is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML. Confirm a somatic RAS-pathway lesion before coding 9946.
nodes.coding_note: This is one of the ten non-reportable mimic points (Pathway §4.9). Forcing an NOS malignant code here would record a cancer that does not exist.

options.label: No somatic secondary lesion; normal karyotype; self-limiting or resolving course — Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferative disease
options.reason: Germline RASopathy (PTPN11, KRAS, NRAS or RIT1) with no somatic secondary lesion, a normal karyotype and a self-limiting course. This is Noonan-spectrum myeloproliferation, not JMML — not a reportable malignancy, no code is emitted (Pathway §3.4, §4.9). Keep under haematology follow-up and re-abstract if a somatic lesion or a clonal cytogenetic abnormality emerges.

options.label: A somatic secondary lesion HAS been documented — a second RAS-pathway hit, monosomy 7 or another clonal marker on the marrow
options.coding_note: Germline RASopathy plus a documented somatic secondary lesion is JMML. The germline variant is recorded as a qualifier, not as the code. ras_pathway_lesion carries the controlled value; record the actual somatic gene or clonal marker verbatim in genotype_annotation, because the controlled vocabulary of Pathway §5.1 has no value for 'somatic secondary lesion, gene unspecified'.

options.label: Somatic testing on the marrow has not been performed — clonality unresolved
options.reason: A germline RASopathy variant with no somatic marrow testing. Clonality is unresolved, so a malignancy is not established: not a reportable malignancy at this point and no code is emitted (Pathway §5.6). Repeat the marrow with somatic RAS-pathway testing and re-abstract if a somatic lesion is found.

nodes.question: Record the fusion or mutation exactly as the report states it.
nodes.capture_label: Genotype as reported (e.g. "CCDC88C::FLT3 by RNA-seq", "ALK fusion by FISH", "monosomy 7 only, RAS panel negative")
nodes.hint: The code does not change, but the genotype is preserved on the case record — otherwise the information is lost permanently.
nodes.coding_note: ICC-2022's 'JMML-like neoplasm' category is NOT adopted (Pathway §5.3.2). RAS-negative JMML phenocopies code 9975 (MDS/MPN, unclassifiable) on their own merits, so 9975 needs no disambiguating note on the code itself.

resolution_logic.coding_note: RAS-negative JMML-like neoplasm recorded as an annotation on 9975.
resolution_logic.upgrade_path: None — no ICD-O-3.2 code exists for this entity. The genotype is preserved on the case record instead.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm, unclassifiable.
nos_fallback.reason: MDS/MPN overlap picture recorded but the CMML, aCML and JMML criteria were not met or could not be established.

nodes.question: Which tier of the CMML supporting-criteria rule does this case satisfy?
nodes.hint: Supporting criteria are: dysplasia in ≥10% of cells in ≥1 lineage, and clonal cytogenetic or molecular evidence. How many you need depends on the monocyte count.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Exclude reactive monocytosis before coding 9945, especially at the ≥1×10⁹/L level. CMUS / CCMUS — the criteria unmet — is not malignant and must not be reported (Pathway §3.10).
nodes.coding_note: CMML-1 (<5% PB / <10% BM blasts) versus CMML-2 (5–19% / 10–19%) is a grade, not a code — both are 9945. WHO-HAEM5 and ICC have converged on the monocyte threshold; there is no divergence to record here (Pathway §5.4).

options.label: Monocytes ≥1×10⁹/L and ≥10% of WBC, blasts under 20%, and AT LEAST ONE supporting criterion — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage, OR clonal cytogenetic/molecular evidence
options.coding_note: The one-supporting-criterion tier (Pathway §3.10). Record which criterion was met on the output block.

options.label: Monocytes 0.5–<1×10⁹/L and ≥10% of WBC, blasts under 20%, and BOTH supporting criteria — dysplasia ≥10% in ≥1 lineage AND clonal cytogenetic/molecular evidence
options.coding_note: The two-supporting-criteria tier (Pathway §3.10). Both are required at this monocyte level.

options.label: Blasts in the CMML-2 range (peripheral 5–19% or marrow 10–19%), criteria otherwise met
options.coding_note: CMML-2. The grade is recorded on the output block; the code stays 9945.

options.label: Monocytes 0.5–<1×10⁹/L with only ONE supporting criterion
options.reason: The two-tier CMML rule is not satisfied: at 0.5–<1×10⁹/L both supporting criteria are required. This is CMUS/CCMUS — not malignant, no code is emitted (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Neither supporting criterion has been assessed — no dysplasia assessment and no cytogenetics
options.upgrade_path: A dysplasia assessment on the marrow and cytogenetics/FISH would establish or exclude 9945.
options.coding_note: The monocytic MDS/MPN picture is real but the CMML criteria are unestablished. 9975 is the NOS parent (Pathway §6 fallback chain).

nodes.question: Confirm that the specific MDS/MPN categories have each been considered and excluded.
nodes.hint: 9975 is a diagnosis of exclusion, not a shortcut. It is also the registry's landing code for RAS-negative JMML phenocopies.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before any clonal eosinophilia code (9964–9967), document exclusion of parasitic infection and HIV. Unresolved secondary cause → do not code as a myeloid neoplasm.
nodes.coding_note: 9975 is distinct from 9960 (MPN, NOS, subgroup Ic). The eosinophilia cascade (9964–9968) and atypical CML (9876) belong to the chronic myeloid / MPN tree, not to this one (Pathway §3.10, §7.1).

options.label: CMML, atypical CML, JMML and MDS/MPN-RS-T all considered and excluded — overlapping myelodysplastic and myeloproliferative features remain
options.coding_note: MDS/MPN, unclassifiable, on its own merits.

options.label: Hypereosinophilia dominates and parasitic infection and HIV have BOTH been excluded and documented
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before any clonal eosinophilia code (9964–9968), document exclusion of parasitic infection and HIV. Unresolved secondary cause → do not code as a myeloid neoplasm.
options.coding_note: The clonal-eosinophilia terminals (9964–9968) are owned by the chronic myeloid / MPN tree and are never emitted from here (Pathway §3.10, §7.1). This branch now hands the case straight to that tree's hard secondary-cause gate, which re-confirms the parasitic and HIV exclusions — one tap, and no path into 9964–9968 bypasses the gate — and then runs the FIP1L1::PDGFRA / PDGFRB / FGFR1 / PCM1::JAK2 cascade. FIP1L1::PDGFRA is CRYPTIC: a normal karyotype does not exclude 9965 (Pathway §5.6).

options.label: Hypereosinophilia with a secondary cause identified — parasitic infection (strongyloides, schistosoma, filariasis, hookworm, toxocara), HIV, drugs, allergy or autoimmune disease
options.reason: The hypereosinophilia has a documented secondary cause. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted. This is the commonest false-positive registration risk in Group I in the UCI catchment (Pathway §3.10, §4.9).

options.label: Reviewed — the overlap picture is reactive or the diagnosis was revised
options.reason: Reviewed as reactive or non-neoplastic rather than an MDS/MPN overlap neoplasm. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted.

nodes.question: Marrow blasts are under 5% and peripheral blasts under 2%. What does the marrow and trephine report support?
nodes.hint: This is refractory cytopenia of childhood territory — the commonest myelodysplastic syndrome of childhood, about 50% of paediatric MDS. Its code is 9985.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Entry point from the acute tree's blast gate (<5% band) and from this tree's own marrow-pattern node. ICC criteria (Pathway §3.5): persistent age-adjusted cytopenia, dysplasia in ≥2 lineages or ≥10% in one, blasts PB <2% / BM <5%, no prior cytotoxic therapy, no fibrosis. About 80% are hypocellular; monosomy 7 in about 20%.

options.label: Persistent age-adjusted cytopenia with dysplasia in ≥2 lineages, or ≥10% dysplasia in a single lineage
Hypocellular marrow with cytopenias — refractory cytopenia of childhood versus severe aplastic anaemia not yet separated
options.coding_note: CD61 or CD41 IHC on the trephine is MANDATORY here — micromegakaryocytes are the feature that separates refractory cytopenia of childhood from severe aplastic anaemia, the key differential (Pathway §3.5).

options.label: Cytopenia only — dysplasia not assessed, no trephine performed
options.coding_note: Without a trephine the aplastic-anaemia differential cannot be closed. Record the omission; it drives the upgrade line.

options.label: Ring sideroblasts prominent on the iron stain
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.

options.label: Reviewed — the cytopenia is fully explained by a non-neoplastic cause and there is no dysplastic clone
options.reason: The cytopenia has a documented non-neoplastic cause and no dysplastic clone was found. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Tick every marker the trephine IHC report calls positive. Tap again for strong, again for weak, again for negative.
nodes.hint: CD61 or CD41 identifies micromegakaryocytes. Their presence is what separates refractory cytopenia of childhood from severe aplastic anaemia.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: CD61 / CD41 IHC on the trephine is mandatory in this differential (Pathway §3.5). A negative panel does not by itself code aplastic anaemia — it routes to the aplastic-anaemia and IBMFS exclusions.

marker_groups.group_label: Megakaryocyte panel — mandatory on the trephine

resolution_logic.coding_note: Micromegakaryocytes with 5–19% blasts is paediatric MDS with excess blasts, not refractory cytopenia of childhood.
Micromegakaryocytes present — a dysplastic megakaryocyte lineage. Refractory cytopenia of childhood territory; the mandatory exclusions come next.
CD61-positive micromegakaryocytes are sufficient — CD41 is the alternative, not an additional requirement.
Fibrosis excludes refractory cytopenia of childhood under the ICC criteria (Pathway §3.5). Re-assess the differential before coding.
No micromegakaryocytes in a hypocellular marrow — severe aplastic anaemia and inherited bone-marrow failure are now the leading differentials.
No marker combination met. The differential is unresolved and must be settled explicitly — do not default to an MDS code.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Myelodysplastic picture recorded but the subtype could not be established.

nodes.question: The marrow is hypocellular without micromegakaryocytes. What does the bone-marrow-failure workup show?
nodes.hint: Chromosome breakage / G2 arrest tests for Fanconi anaemia; telomere length for dyskeratosis congenita and the telomere biology disorders; consider Shwachman-Diamond.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Two of the ten non-reportable mimic points sit here: severe aplastic anaemia and inherited bone-marrow-failure syndromes (Pathway §4.9). Neither may be recorded as an MDS code.

options.label: Hypocellular marrow, no micromegakaryocytes, no dysplasia, normal cytogenetics — severe aplastic anaemia
options.reason: Severe aplastic anaemia — the key differential of refractory cytopenia of childhood. Not a reportable malignancy, no code is emitted (Pathway §3.5, §4.9). Re-abstract if dysplasia, micromegakaryocytes or a clonal cytogenetic abnormality emerge on follow-up.

options.label: Chromosome breakage / G2 arrest abnormal, telomeres short, or a syndromic phenotype — inherited bone-marrow-failure syndrome (Fanconi anaemia, dyskeratosis congenita, Shwachman-Diamond)
options.reason: Inherited bone-marrow-failure syndrome. Not reportable as a myelodysplastic syndrome — no code is emitted; refer to the genetics and haematology services (Pathway §4.9). Re-abstract if the patient later develops MDS or acute leukaemia.

options.label: Dysplasia and/or a clonal cytogenetic abnormality (for example monosomy 7) is present after all
options.coding_note: A clone changes the answer — continue down the myelodysplastic pathway.

options.label: Breakage and telomere testing are not available at this facility — the differential is unresolved
options.reason: Bone-marrow failure with no dysplasia, no micromegakaryocytes and no clonal marker, and with inherited-bone-marrow-failure testing unavailable. A myelodysplastic syndrome is not established, so no code is emitted. Refer for a bone-marrow-failure workup and re-abstract if dysplasia or a clone emerges.

nodes.question: Marrow blasts are 5–19% (peripheral 2–19%). What does the marrow report support?
nodes.hint: Paediatric MDS with excess blasts stays a 5–19% band. ICC's separate MDS/AML 10–19% category does not apply under 18 years.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Entry point from the acute tree's blast gate (5–19% band). Registry arbitration (Pathway §5.4): ICC is used for blast thresholds AND for the <18-years MDS/AML exclusion — a child in the 10–19% band with a dysplastic marrow is paediatric MDS-EB (9983), not MDS/AML.

options.label: Dysplasia documented — continue the mandatory paediatric MDS exclusions (reversible causes, prior therapy, germline predisposition, IBMFS)
Marrow report gives a blast count only — dysplasia not assessed and no trephine performed
options.coding_note: Record the omission. Without a dysplasia assessment the case cannot be separated from a hypoplastic acute leukaemia or from marrow recovery.

options.label: The marrow reads as an acute picture rather than dysplasia — sheets of blasts, no maturation
options.coding_note: Return to the acute tree and assign lineage. A missed AML/APL is the costlier error (Pathway §7.1).

options.label: No dysplasia — the blast increase and cytopenia are explained by a recovering marrow, B12/folate deficiency or infection
options.reason: The blast increase is reactive — marrow recovery, nutritional deficiency or infection — with no dysplastic clone. Not a reportable malignancy, no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

nodes.question: Have the reversible causes of cytopenia and dysplasia-like change been excluded and documented?
nodes.hint: Uganda addition to the ICC criteria: exclude nutritional (B12, folate, iron) and HIV-related cytopenia and macrocytosis BEFORE any paediatric MDS code.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Nutritional (B12 / folate / iron) deficiency, HIV, chronic infection and drug effect all mimic myelodysplasia. Exclude them and document the exclusion before coding — they are non-reportable terminals, not NOS codes (Pathway §3.5, §4.9).
nodes.coding_note: This gate does not change the code; it decides whether there is a code at all. Its result is carried on the output block.

options.label: B12 / folate / iron deficiency, HIV, chronic infection and drug effect all excluded and documented
Nutritional deficiency (B12, folate or iron) identified and the cytopenia or macrocytosis is attributable to it
options.reason: Nutritional deficiency accounts for the macrocytosis and dysplasia-like change. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §3.5, §4.9). Re-abstract if the picture persists after replacement.

options.label: HIV-related cytopenia or HIV-associated marrow change accounts for the picture
options.reason: HIV-related marrow change accounts for the cytopenia and dysplasia-like features. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §3.5, §4.9).

options.label: Malaria or HIV hypersplenism accounts for the splenomegaly and cytopenias
options.reason: Hypersplenism from malaria or HIV accounts for the splenomegaly and cytopenias. Not a reportable malignancy — no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).

options.label: Not assessed — the file does not document these exclusions
options.coding_note: The case can still be coded, but the omission is recorded and appears as a workup row on the output block. Skipping this step is the largest single false-positive registration risk in this group.

nodes.question: Has this patient had prior cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy?
nodes.hint: 'No prior cytotoxic therapy' is one of the ICC criteria for refractory cytopenia of childhood, so it is asked explicitly.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Prior cytotoxic therapy is a qualifier on the underlying neoplasm (ELN 2022), not a separate entity. Code the underlying subtype and set the qualifier rather than defaulting to 9920/9987.
nodes.coding_note: Therapy-related disease is a QUALIFIER, not a code (Pathway §4.8, §5.3.7). This tree never routes to 9987 or 9920 — both are closed as terminals. Code the underlying MDS subtype and set the qualifier.

options.label: No prior cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy
options.coding_note: Satisfies the ICC 'no prior cytotoxic therapy' criterion for refractory cytopenia of childhood.

options.label: Prior cytotoxic chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy documented
options.coding_note: The qualifier is recorded on the output block. Continue and code the underlying MDS entity — never 9987, never 9920. The ICC criteria for refractory cytopenia of childhood are not met once prior cytotoxic therapy is documented, so 9985 is not available on this branch.

options.label: Not documented in the file

nodes.question: What germline predisposition and inherited-bone-marrow-failure testing does the file document?
nodes.hint: About 20% of refractory cytopenia of childhood has an underlying germline hit, so this is high-yield. It does not change the code — it must be recorded.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Mandatory pre-condition before any sporadic paediatric MDS code (Pathway §3.5): a germline predisposition screen (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ANKRD26, ETV6) and an IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage / G2 arrest, telomere length; consider Shwachman-Diamond). Recorded as a modifier on the output block.

options.label: Germline panel performed — no predisposition variant; breakage and telomere testing normal
Germline GATA2 variant identified
options.coding_note: GATA2 deficiency is the commonest germline predisposition in paediatric MDS with monosomy 7. It is a modifier, not a code — the MDS subtype still sets the code.

options.label: Germline SAMD9 or SAMD9L variant identified
options.coding_note: SAMD9/SAMD9L (MIRAGE, ataxia-pancytopenia) is associated with monosomy 7 and with somatic reversion. Modifier only.

options.label: Germline RUNX1, ETV6 or ANKRD26 variant identified
options.coding_note: Familial platelet disorder with predisposition to myeloid malignancy. Modifier only — the code is still the MDS subtype.

options.label: Chromosome breakage / G2 arrest abnormal, or telomeres short — inherited bone-marrow-failure syndrome
options.reason: Inherited bone-marrow-failure syndrome (Fanconi anaemia, dyskeratosis congenita or a related telomere biology disorder). Not reportable as a myelodysplastic syndrome — no code is emitted; refer to genetics and haematology (Pathway §3.5, §4.9). Re-abstract if the patient later develops MDS or acute leukaemia.

options.label: Germline and IBMFS testing are not available at this facility
options.coding_note: The code is unchanged, but the omission MUST be recorded — it appears as a workup row and an upgrade line on the output block (Pathway §5.6).

nodes.question: Which cytogenetic / FISH finding does the report give?
nodes.hint: Cytogenetics in paediatric MDS are prognostic and supporting; only isolated del(5q) is code-defining, and it is confirmed with the blast count and the dysplasia pattern.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: Monosomy 7 is the commonest abnormality in paediatric MDS (~20% of refractory cytopenia of childhood) and is NOT code-defining. SEER over-counting rule (Pathway §3.5): within the MDS family code only the first subtype diagnosed — do not re-abstract a later, more specific subtype.

options.finding: Monosomy 7 or del(7q)
options.coding_note: Supporting, not defining. It appears in refractory cytopenia of childhood, in paediatric MDS-EB, in GATA2 deficiency and in JMML alike.

options.finding: Isolated del(5q)
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
options.coding_note: 9986 requires the deletion to be ISOLATED and the blast count to be under 5%. Both are confirmed at the next two steps before the code is emitted.

options.finding: Complex karyotype — three or more abnormalities
options.coding_note: Prognostically adverse, not code-defining within the MDS family.

options.finding: Trisomy 8, del(20q), or another single abnormality
Karyotype normal
options.coding_note: A normal karyotype does not exclude a myelodysplastic syndrome — the diagnosis rests on persistent cytopenia plus dysplasia, not on a clone.

options.finding: An AML-defining abnormality — PML::RARA, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, KMT2A-r, NUP98-r or MECOM-r
options.coding_note: This is not a myelodysplastic syndrome. Under WHO-HAEM5 a defining abnormality makes the case AML at any blast percentage; ICC applies a ≥10% floor to the same list. Either way the case leaves this tree for the acute tree.

options.finding: Cytogenetics not performed, or unavailable at this facility
options.coding_note: "Cytogenetics unavailable at UCI" is a legitimate, permanent terminal state — but it must be recorded as such, not passed off as a completed workup. 9986 is not reachable without it.

options.finding: MDS-defining cytogenetics after prior cytotoxic chemotherapy or radiotherapy, subtype otherwise unclassified
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Prior cytotoxic therapy is a qualifier on the underlying neoplasm (ELN 2022), not a separate entity. Code the underlying subtype and set the qualifier rather than defaulting to 9920/9987.
options.coding_note: DO NOT CODE 9987. Therapy-related MDS is a qualifier on the underlying diagnosis, not a terminal (Pathway §4.8, §5.3.7). 9989 carries the subtype-unclassified MDS; therapy_related_qualifier carries the relationship.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Myelodysplastic picture recorded but the subtype could not be established.

nodes.question: Marrow blast percentage (of ALL nucleated marrow cells)?
nodes.hint: The denominator is all nucleated cells, not non-erythroid cells. If the acute tree already recorded a blast count, re-enter the same value — this is the gate that fixes the code. Tick 'not documented' rather than guessing.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: The blast band is what separates 9983 from the low-blast MDS codes. The all-nucleated-cell denominator retires the old erythroid/myeloid split (Pathway §2.2).

override_when.coding_note: A defining AML abnormality overrides the blast threshold under WHO-HAEM5; ICC applies a ≥10% floor to the same list. Either way this is not a myelodysplastic syndrome.

bands.coding_note: ≥20% is acute leukaemia under both WHO-HAEM5 and ICC — no divergence. Leave the MDS tree and assign lineage.

ICC's MDS/AML 10–19% category is explicitly EXCLUDED under 18 years (Pathway §5.4). In a child a dysplastic marrow at 10–19% blasts is paediatric MDS with excess blasts — 9983 — not MDS/AML. In an adult patient this band would be MDS/AML under ICC; flag for review if the patient is 18 or over.
bands.upgrade_path: None on the blast count. Cytogenetics/FISH would add prognostic detail; the code is unchanged.

bands.coding_note: Paediatric MDS with excess blasts: BM 5–19%, PB 2–19% (Pathway §3.5). The 5–19% band is retained for children under both the ICC arbitration and the registry's code list.
bands.upgrade_path: None on the blast count. Cytogenetics/FISH would add prognostic detail; the code is unchanged.

bands.coding_note: BM <5% / PB <2% — low-blast territory. The dysplasia pattern now chooses between 9985, 9980, 9982, 9993, 9986 and 9989.
Blast percentage undocumented. Do not assume the excess-blast band — resolve the case on the dysplasia pattern and record the missing blast count as an upgrade.

nos_fallback.name: Myelodysplastic syndrome, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: Myelodysplastic picture recorded but the subtype could not be established.

nodes.question: Which dysplasia pattern does the marrow and trephine report describe?
nodes.hint: Blasts are under 5% in the marrow and under 2% in the blood. The dysplasia pattern now chooses the code.
nodes.clinical_alert: ⚠️ Before coding paediatric MDS, document germline predisposition testing (GATA2, SAMD9/SAMD9L, RUNX1, ETV6, ANKRD26) and IBMFS exclusion (chromosome breakage, telomere length). These do not change the code but must be recorded.
nodes.coding_note: 9985 is THE paediatric refractory-cytopenia-of-childhood code and the commonest myelodysplastic syndrome of childhood, about 50% (Pathway §3.5). SEER lists 'refractory cytopenia of childhood' and 'childhood MDS with low blasts' as explicit alternate names for 9985/3.

options.descriptor: Dysplasia in ≥2 lineages, or ≥10% dysplasia in a single lineage, with persistent age-adjusted cytopenia — refractory cytopenia of childhood
options.coding_note: Refractory cytopenia of childhood / childhood MDS with low blasts. About 80% are hypocellular with patchy erythroid islands; monosomy 7 in about 20%. CD61/CD41 IHC must have separated this from severe aplastic anaemia.
options.upgrade_path: None on the code. Germline predisposition and IBMFS results, if still outstanding, are recorded as modifiers.

options.descriptor: Single-lineage dysplasia, anaemia predominant, no ring sideroblasts
options.coding_note: 9980 (refractory anaemia) is a FAB-era term retained for the single-lineage presentation; the retired codes 9991 (refractory neutropenia) and 9992 (refractory thrombocytopenia) alias to it. In a child, review whether the multilineage criteria are in fact met — 9985 is the commoner paediatric assignment.
options.upgrade_path: A repeat trephine assessing all three lineages would establish whether the case is in fact 9985.

options.descriptor: Ring sideroblasts ≥15% (or ≥5% with SF3B1), single-lineage dysplasia
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
options.coding_note: Under 1% of paediatric myelodysplastic syndromes. Kept reachable for the genuine rare paediatric case, with the age-implausibility warning attached (Pathway §7.5).

options.descriptor: Ring sideroblasts with MULTILINEAGE dysplasia, with or without SF3B1
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
options.coding_note: 9993 was ADDED in ICD-O-3.2 (Pathway §5.7). Adult-predominant; kept reachable with the age-implausibility warning.

options.descriptor: Isolated del(5q) with macrocytic anaemia and preserved or raised platelets
options.clinical_alert: ⚠️ This entity is described almost exclusively in adults. Confirm independently in a paediatric patient and flag for senior pathology review before finalising.
options.coding_note: The deletion must be ISOLATED and the blasts under 5%. Rare in children; kept reachable with the age-implausibility warning.

options.descriptor: Dysplasia documented but the subtype is not stated, or the lineages involved are not recorded
options.coding_note: 9989 is the MDS fallback when the subtype is undocumented. It is a real terminal, not a placeholder — but the missing detail is listed as an upgrade.
options.upgrade_path: A trephine reporting dysplasia by lineage would establish 9985 or 9980; an iron stain would establish 9982 or 9993; cytogenetics would establish 9986.

options.descriptor: Reviewed — no dysplasia; the cytopenia is non-neoplastic
options.reason: No dysplastic clone on review — the cytopenia is non-neoplastic. Not a reportable malignancy, no code is emitted (Pathway §4.9).
